74345.subject: Government
74345.question_text: The First-Past-the-Post system of voting is also referred to as
74345.explanation: The First-Past-The-Post (FPTP) system is a common electoral system where the candidate who receives the most votes wins, even if they do not receive an absolute majority (more than 50%). "Simple majority" refers to having more votes than any other single candidate.

74346.subject: Government
74346.question_text: A community that cooperates and harnesses its resources together is said to be practising
74346.explanation: The term communalism is a social or economic system where members of a community work together for their mutual benefit. This is an ideology and mode of production where a particular community collectively owns, manages and controls resources and the means of production. In this system, members live close together, support one another and pool their resources to pursue common goals.

74419.subject: Government
74419.question_text: The African leaders formally marked the end of the Organisation of African Unity and replaced it with the African Union in
74419.explanation: On this date, the African Union (AU) was officially launched at the Durban Summit in South Africa, formally replacing the Organisation of African Unity (OAU), which had been in existence since 1963.

74420.subject: Government
74420.question_text: A permanent structure that facilitates continuity in governance is the
74420.explanation:
The civil service is the permanent administrative arm of the government, composed of non-elected, career officials who remain in office regardless of changes in political leadership.

The civil service has several key features that ensure a government continues to function smoothly even when political leaders change:

  • Permanence: Unlike elected officials (the political class) whose tenure is limited by elections, civil servants have permanent careers and job security.

  • Institutional Memory: Because they serve for long periods, civil servants preserve the "memory" of how government programs operate to provide stability during political transitions.

  • Political Neutrality: Civil servants are expected to be non-partisan, serving whichever government is in power with equal dedication to ensure no breakdown in state activities.

  • Policy Implementation: While politicians formulate policies, the civil service is the "engine room" that actually translates those policies into concrete actions and public services.

74421.subject: Government
74421.question_text: The two constitutions that provided for the election of four legislative members were
74421.explanation:
The Clifford Constitution introduced the elective principle for the first time. It provided for 4 elected members: 3 for Lagos and 1 for Calabar.Richard Constitution1946

The Richards Constitution retained the elective principle from the 1922 constitution. It continued to provide for 4 elected members: 3 for Lagos and 1 for Calabar.

74422.subject: Government
74422.question_text: One of the functions of Public Corporation is to
74422.explanation:
The primary purpose of a public corporation is to handle services that are vital to the public welfare but may be too capital-intensive for private individuals. They are set up to provide necessities such as water, electricity and telecommunications at a reduced cost to the public.

Unlike private businesses, their primary aim is not profit-making, but rather the social and economic development of the country.

74423.subject: Government
74423.question_text: The appointments of qualified personnel into any federal establishment as a minister were to reflect the principle of
74423.explanation:
In Nigeria, the appointment of ministers must reflect the Federal Character principle to ensure balanced representation from across the country.

The Nigerian Constitution mandates that the President must appoint at least one minister from each state of the federation to satisfy this requirement. This principle was introduced in the 1979 Constitution to prevent any single ethnic or regional group from dominating the government and to promote national unity.

 The Federal Character Commission was established to monitor and enforce this fair distribution of political and bureaucratic positions.

74424.subject: Government
74424.question_text: The pioneer president of the Action Group was
74424.explanation:
Chief Obafemi Awolowo was the founder and first leader of the Action Group (AG), which was established in March 1951. The party grew out of a cultural organisation called Egbe Omo Oduduwa and became a major political force in the Western Region.

Awolowo led the party through the pre-independence era and served as the first Premier of the Western Region starting in 1954.

74425.subject: Government
74425.explanation: Nigeria is a member of the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), having joined in 1971. Nigeria is NOT a member of the ARAB League, EAC (East African Community) or NATO.

74426.subject: Government
74426.question_text: The Nigerian Supreme Court became the highest court of appeal in the
74426.explanation: The 1963 Republican Constitution established the Supreme Court of Nigeria as the highest court of appeal. This abolished the previous system where appeals went to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in the United Kingdom. This marked Nigeria's full judicial sovereignty.

74427.subject: Government
74427.question_text: One of the major reasons for colonialism in Africa was
74427.explanation:
A major driving force for European colonialism in Africa was economic interest, including the pursuit of raw materials, new markets and the exploitation of natural resources like gold and diamonds.

While religious and humanitarian factors were used as public justifications, the primary motivation was the material greed and material exploitation of the continent.

74428.subject: Government
74428.question_text: One major feature of Nigerian foreign policy is
74428.explanation: A major feature of Nigerian foreign policy since independence is non-alignment. This means Nigeria chose not to formally ally itself with either the Western (USA) or Eastern (Soviet) blocs during the Cold War, maintaining independence in its international relations.

options.text: non-alignment with any of the power blocs

74429.subject: Government
74429.question_text: Which of these is a professional pressure group in Nigeria?
74429.explanation:
The Nigerian Union of Teachers (NUT) is a professional pressure group because it represents the specific interests of people in the teaching profession.

  • NLC: Is the central labour organisation 

  • MAN: Represents manufacturers/employers.

  • Arewa Consultative Forum: Is a socio-cultural and political group.

74430.subject: Government
74430.question_text: Local Government Areas in Nigeria are by act of the 1999 constitution a/ an
74430.explanation:
Section 7 of the 1999 Constitution guarantees the existence of local government councils as the third tier of government. The Constitution prescribes their structure, finance and functions, aiming for them to be responsive and accountable to citizens at the grassroots level.

While they are theoretically autonomous, in practice they struggle with financial independence because of the State Joint Local Government Account (SJLGA).

74431.subject: Government
74431.question_text: The fusion of executive and legislative powers is a core feature of
74431.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the executive branch (the Prime Minister and Cabinet) is drawn directly from the legislative branch (Parliament). This creates a "fusion of powers" rather than a strict separation.

74433.subject: Government
74433.question_text: A proposal discussed in the parliament and passed for signing to become a law is a
74433.explanation: A bill is a draft or a formal proposal for a new law (or a change to an existing one) that is introduced and discussed in a legislature, such as a parliament. It only becomes an act (law) after it has been passed by the legislature and received the required signature or assent from the head of state.

74434.subject: Government
74434.question_text: The highest court in the Hausa-Fulani political system was presided by
74434.explanation: In the pre-colonial Hausa-Fulani political system, the Emir held supreme executive, legislative and judicial powers. While minor cases were handled in local Alkali courts presided over by trained Islamic judges, the Emir's Court served as the highest court in the land and the final court of appeal.

74435.subject: Government
74435.question_text: The New Partnership for Africa's Development (NEPAD) was established in
74435.explanation: The New Partnership for Africa's Development (NEPAD) was officially adopted by African Heads of State and Government in July 2001 during a summit in Lusaka, Zambia. It was formed through the merger of two existing plans: the Millennium Partnership for Africa's Recovery Programme (MAP) and the OMEGA Plan.

74436.subject: Government
74436.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a duty of citizens in a state?
74436.explanation:
Spying on the state is not a duty; it is considered an act of treason or a criminal offence against the state. Common duties and responsibilities of citizens include:

  • Payment of taxes: Promptly declaring income and paying required levies to fund government services.

  • Voting at elections: Participating in the selection of political leaders.

  • Prevention of crimes: Reporting suspected criminal activities to the appropriate authorities.

74437.subject: Government
74437.explanation: In a confederal system (or confederation), power is highly decentralised. The central government is weak, limited to coordinating common interests like defence or foreign affairs, while the component units (states) remain strong and retain their individual sovereignty.

74438.subject: Government
74438.question_text: When a constitution requires a special organ or a more difficult amendment procedure, such constitution is applicable in which system of government?
74438.explanation: When a constitution requires a "special organ" or a "more difficult amendment procedure," it is known as a rigid constitution. This is a hallmark of a federal system of government, where the constitution is supreme and designed to protect the division of power between the central government and the constituent states.

74575.subject: Government
74575.question_text: The NPN presidential candidate in the Second Republic was
74575.explanation: During Nigeria's Second Republic, Alhaji Shehu Shagari was the presidential candidate for the National Party of Nigeria (NPN). He won the 1979 election and became the first executive president of Nigeria.

74576.subject: Government
74576.question_text: The detection, prevention and investigation of criminal activities in Nigeria is the primary responsibility of the
74576.explanation: In Nigeria, the Police (specifically the Nigeria Police Force) have the primary constitutional responsibility for the detection, prevention and investigation of criminal activities. While citizens and vigilantes can assist, the formal legal authority for investigation lies with the police.

74577.subject: Government
74577.question_text: The essence of the doctrine of separation of powers is to prevent
74577.explanation: The primary goal of separating powers into Executive, Legislative and Judicial branches is to create checks and balances, ensuring that no single branch becomes too powerful or tyrannical.

74578.subject: Government
74578.question_text: The determinants of a country's foreign policy are often influenced by
74578.explanation: While many factors play a role, economic interests, such as trade agreements and resource access, are central to how a country interacts with others and shapes its foreign policy.

74579.subject: Government
74579.question_text: The system of government in which the central  and component units possess coordinated powers is
74579.explanation: In a Federal system, power is constitutionally divided and shared between a central (national) government and various component units (like states or provinces). The term "coordinated powers" refers to the fact that both levels of government are supreme within their own spheres of influence and must work in tandem.

74580.subject: Government
74580.question_text: The primary function of the judiciary is to
74580.explanation: In a standard democratic system governed by the separation of powers, each branch of government has a distinct and primary role. The judiciary is tasked with explaining and clarifying the meaning of laws passed by the legislature.

74581.subject: Government
74581.question_text: The Commonwealth Games were last hosted by Nigeria in
74581.explanation: Nigeria has never hosted the Commonwealth Games.

options.text: Nigeria has never hosted the commonwealth games

74582.subject: Government
74582.question_text: An organised group of citizens acting together and seeking to obtain the control of government is a
74582.explanation: A political party is defined as an organised group of citizens who share similar political aims and seek to obtain control of the government by getting their candidates elected to public office.

74583.subject: Government
74583.question_text: Democracy is a system in which the
74583.explanation: Democracy is a system based on the principle of majority rule, where political decisions are made through voting. In a healthy democracy, this is balanced with minority rights to ensure that smaller groups are protected from "the tyranny of the majority".

74584.subject: Government
74584.explanation: Sovereignty is considered one of the most important and essential characteristics of a state. It refers to the state's supreme authority over its territory and its independence from external control. Other essential elements of a state include a defined territory, a population, and a legitimate government.

74585.subject: Government
74585.question_text: The authority of a leader derived from a constitution is
74585.explanation: This refers to authority derived from a system of laws and a constitution, rather than from personal charisma or ancient tradition.

74586.subject: Government
74586.question_text: Census controversy was one of the factors that contributed to the military intervention in
74586.explanation: The census controversy (specifically the disputed 1963 census) was one of the major factors—alongside widespread electoral malpractice in the Western Region—that created the political instability leading to Nigeria's first military intervention on January 15, 1966.

74587.subject: Government
74587.question_text: The African Union came into existence in 2002 when it replaced the
74587.explanation: The AU officially replaced the OAU (established in 1963) in July 2002 at the Durban summit.

74588.subject: Government
74588.question_text: To ensure political neutrality of civil service, members must
74588.explanation: To ensure they remain impartial and serve any government regardless of the party in power, civil servants must avoid active involvement in political parties.

74589.subject: Government
74589.question_text: Public opinion allows an organised government to
74589.explanation: Public opinion allows governments to obtain input and communication from the people they represent.

options.text: infringe the rights of its opponents
find out what the public thinks of its activities

74590.subject: Government
74590.question_text: The Nigeria Railway Corporation is an example of
74590.explanation: The NRC is a state-owned enterprise with the exclusive right to operate railways in Nigeria.

74591.subject: Government
74591.question_text: The Head of the Army in the Yoruba political kingdom is
74591.explanation: This title was given to the generalissimo or war general of the old Oyo Empire.

74593.subject: Government
74593.question_text: The longest and most expensive military transition programme in Nigeria was under
74593.explanation: While General Yakubu Gowon's transition was prolonged, Babangida's transition program (1987–1993) is widely cited in political studies as the longest and most expensive in Nigeria's history due to its multiple postponements, creation of political parties by the government and the building of party secretariats in every local government area.

74595.subject: Government
74595.explanation:
Sovereignty is the supreme power and authority of a state over its own affairs. This is the most accurate definition because it encompasses two key dimensions:

  1. Internal Sovereignty: The power of a state to make and enforce laws within its own borders without interference from internal groups or individuals.

  2. External Sovereignty: The right of a state to exist independently and manage its own foreign policy without being dictated to by other nations.

options.text: the supreme power of a state to use force in order to enforce obedience
the supreme power of a state to negotiate with other states
the supreme power of a state to govern other nations
the supreme power and authority of a state over its own affairs

74597.subject: Government
74597.question_text: A major argument against the First Republic parties is
74597.explanation:
The political parties of the First Republic (1960–1966) are most heavily criticised for being ethnically based and regionally focused. Instead of operating as national entities with a broad country-wide appeal, the three major parties were tied directly to specific regions and ethnic groups:

  • NPC (Northern People's Congress): Rooted in the Northern Region and primarily representing Hausa-Fulani interests.

  • NCNC (National Council of Nigerian Citizens): While initially more national, it became increasingly associated with the Eastern Region and the Igbo people.

  • AG (Action Group): Based in the Western Region and largely representing Yoruba interests.

This "tripartite federal structure" led to a "winner-takes-all" political culture where parties prioritised their own regions over national unity, ultimately resulting in the political instability that led to the 1966 coup.

74599.subject: Government
74599.question_text: Public corporations were established by an act of
74599.explanation: A public corporation is a government-owned enterprise established by a specific Act of Parliament (or a statute/decree) to provide essential services to the public. These corporations are "statutory bodies," meaning they are created by law. The Act of Parliament defines their specific powers, functions and duties

74600.subject: Government
74600.question_text: The most popular method employed by pressure groups is
74600.explanation:
Lobbying is considered the most popular and major method used by pressure groups because it involves direct interaction with legislators and policymakers to influence decisions before they become law.  It can include sending letters, providing research data, making presentations, or face-to-face meetings with government officials.

While strikes are a powerful tool used by labour unions, they are a "method of last resort" when persuasion fails. Lobbying is the day-to-day, ongoing activity of most successful pressure groups.

74601.subject: Government
74601.question_text: The elective principle was first introduced under
74601.explanation: The Clifford Constitution of 1922 was the first to introduce the elective principle in Nigeria. This led to the first-ever elections into the Legislative Council, with three seats for Lagos and one seat for Calabar. The introduction of this principle awakened political consciousness, encouraged the formation of the first political parties (such as the NNDP), and increased the tempo of nationalism.

74602.subject: Government
74602.question_text: One of the key characteristics of the civil service is
74602.explanation: Anonymity is a core principle of the civil service, meaning that civil servants should neither be blamed nor praised in public for the successes or failures of government policy. Other standard characteristics include permanence (stable employment), neutrality (staying apolitical), and impartiality (treating all citizens equally).

74604.subject: Government
74604.question_text: Laws made by the local government, public corporations and ministries is a
74604.explanation: Laws enacted by local authorities, public corporations or professional bodies are called bye-laws. These are limited to the specific area or jurisdiction of the body that created them, such as a law passed by a city council regarding local markets.

74606.subject: Government
74606.question_text: The group that had the best egalitarian traditional political system is the
74606.explanation: Unlike the centralised monarchies of the Yoruba or Hausa, the Igbo traditional political system was decentralised and "acephalous" (lacking a single central head). Power was exercised through a council of elders, age grades, and general assemblies by consensus, emphasising an egalitarian and "ultra-democratic" social structure.

74607.subject: Government
74607.question_text: Nigeria applies soft diplomacy in Africa through
74607.explanation: Nigeria applies soft diplomacy through the Nigerian Technical Aid Corps (TAC), which sends Nigerian professionals (doctors, engineers, teachers) to assist other African, Caribbean and Pacific countries. This programme aims to share Nigeria's human resources to foster development and strengthen diplomatic ties without using military or economic coercion.

74608.subject: Government
74608.question_text: The proto-nationalism before the Second World War was characterised by the
74608.explanation:
Proto-nationalism refers to the early stage of nationalist movements in Africa before the World War II. During this period, nationalist activities were mainly led by:

  • Western-educated elites

  • Lawyers

  • Journalists

  • Teachers

  • Clergy

These educated elements used newspapers, petitions and constitutional agitation to demand reforms from the colonial government. In Nigeria, early nationalist figures like Herbert Macaulay and Nnamdi Azikiwe were part of this educated elite class.

74609.subject: Government
74609.question_text: The main objectives of African Union is to
74609.explanation: The AU's primary goals are to achieve greater unity among African countries and to accelerate the political and socio-economic integration of the continent. It focuses on peace, security and stability as a foundation for economic development.

options.text: regulate business transactions within the international community among members
promote co-operation and economic development  among members
oversee the free flow of political engagement in Africa and developed nations
settle disputes among South East Asia countries

74610.subject: Government
74610.question_text: A type of constitution where the procedure for its amendment is enshrined in it is a
74610.explanation: A rigid constitution is one where the procedure for its amendment is difficult and enshrined within the document. Its amendment requires a special majority (e.g., two-thirds) in the legislature.

74611.subject: Government
74611.question_text: A form of government where the ultimate authority to govern is vested with the people is
74611.explanation: Democracy is a system of government where the ultimate power is vested in the people, who exercise it directly or through freely elected representatives.

74612.subject: Government
74612.question_text: The right to vote and be voted in an election is
74612.explanation: The right to vote and be voted for in an election is known as the franchise.

74613.subject: Government
74613.question_text: The main reason for military intervention in Nigerian politics is the
74613.explanation: The primary reason cited for military intervention in Nigerian politics has been the perceived failure or incapacity of civilian governments to manage the economy, maintain order or curb corruption.

options.text: perceived incapability of civilians to govern

74614.subject: Government
74614.question_text: The coordination and unification of the petroleum policies of its members is one of the main objectives of
74614.explanation:
OPEC stands for the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries. It was founded in 1960 with the specific goal of managing the supply of oil in an effort to set the price of oil on the world market.

The primary objectives of OPEC are:

  • Coordination and Unification: Aligning the petroleum policies of member countries to ensure stability in the oil market.

  • Price Stability: Preventing fluctuations that could be harmful to both producers and consumers.

  • Steady Income: Securing an efficient, economic, and regular supply of petroleum to consuming nations and a fair return on capital for those investing in the petroleum industry.

74615.subject: Government
74615.question_text: Which of the following factors can limit the application of the rule of law?
74615.explanation:
The rule of law requires that justice be delivered fairly and within a reasonable timeframe. When courts are overwhelmed with a backlog of cases, it creates significant barriers to its application:

  • Delayed Justice: A core tenet of the rule of law is that "justice delayed is justice denied." High caseloads mean litigants may wait years for a hearing, making the legal system ineffective for resolving urgent disputes.

  • Loss of Public Confidence: Continuous delays and "nonsense" results from backlogs can erode the public's trust in the judiciary and the fairness of laws.

  • Weakened Enforcement: Large backlogs prevent the timely enforcement of rights, which directly weakens the democratic principle that everyone is subject to and protected by the law.

74616.subject: Government
74616.question_text: A system in which more than two political parties contest for an election is referred to as
74616.explanation: In a multi-party system, more than two distinct political parties exist, are officially recognised, and regularly compete for and win public offices. This system provides voters with a wider range of choices compared to other systems.

74617.subject: Government
74617.question_text: The Independent National Electoral Commission is responsible for
74617.explanation:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is responsible for (B) conducting general elections.

Key Functions of INEC:

  • Electoral Management: Its primary role is to organise, undertake, and supervise elections for the offices of the President, Governors, and members of the National and State Assemblies.

  • Voter Registration: It registers qualified voters and maintains the national register of voters.

  • Party Regulation: It registers political parties and monitors their organization and finances.

74618.subject: Government
74618.explanation: Public corporations are government-owned establishments created through specific Acts of Parliament (statutes), decrees, or edicts. They are established to provide essential social and welfare services to the public, such as water and electricity. They are separate legal entities, meaning they can sue and be sued in their own name. Their primary goal is public service rather than making a profit.

74619.subject: Government
74619.question_text: The use of Prime Minister as the head of Government is associated with which system of governance?
74619.explanation: The use of a Prime Minister as the head of government is the defining feature of a Parliamentary system (also known as the Westminster model). In this system, there is usually a distinction between the Head of State (a Monarch or President with ceremonial powers) and the Head of Government (the Prime Minister, who holds executive power).

74620.subject: Government
74620.question_text: The institution of government that interprets laws made by the legislature is
74620.explanation:
Under the doctrine of the separation of powers, each branch has a specific role:

  • Legislature: Makes the laws.

  • Executive: Enforces or puts the laws into operation.

  • Judiciary: Interprets, defends and applies the law to specific cases.

74621.subject: Government
74621.question_text: Citizenship is best defined as a member of a state who is legally and constitutionally
74621.explanation: Citizenship is best defined as a member of a state who is legally and constitutionally recognised as having the full rights and responsibilities of that state. Recognition by the law allows a person to enjoy civil and political rights, such as voting.

74622.subject: Government
74622.question_text: Fascism and Nazism are ideologies that were promoted respectively by
74622.explanation: Fascism and Nazism were two far-right political ideologies that rose to prominence in Europe during the interwar period. Promoted by Benito Mussolini in Italy. He founded the National Fascist Party in 1921 and became the dictator of Italy. Nazism, short for National Socialism, was the German variant of fascism promoted by Adolf Hitler. While similar to Italian fascism in its authoritarianism, Nazism placed a much heavier emphasis on racial purity and the superiority of the "Aryan" race.

74623.subject: Government
74623.question_text: The process by which citizens get involved in the political activities and decision-making of their country is
74623.explanation:
The process by which citizens get involved in the political activities and decision-making of their country is known as political participation. It describes a broad range of voluntary activities intended to influence public policy and the selection of political leaders. While voting is the most frequent form, political participation also includes working on campaigns, joining political parties, contacting public officials, protesting and petitioning.

It is considered vital for a healthy democracy because it ensures the government hears the voices of its citizens and remains accountable to them.

74624.subject: Government
74624.question_text: The age qualifications of members of the Senate and House of Representatives under the 1979 constitution were
74624.explanation:
Under the 1979 Constitution of Nigeria, specific age requirements were set for those wishing to contest for seats in the National Assembly:

  • Senate: A candidate was required to have attained the age of 30 years.

  • House of Representatives: A candidate was required to have attained the age of 21 years.

These requirements changed in later constitutions (such as the 1999 Constitution), which raised the ages to 35 for the Senate and 30 for the House of Representatives.

74625.subject: Government
74625.question_text: The War Against Indiscipline campaign was launched by the military regime of
74625.explanation:
The War Against Indiscipline (WAI) was a mass mobilisation program in Nigeria aimed at correcting social maladjustment and corruption. It was officially launched in March 1984. It was a hallmark initiative of the military government of Major General Muhammadu Buhari (1983–1985). The program was announced by his second-in-command, Brigadier General Tunde Idiagbon.

The campaign promoted orderliness, such as queuing correctly for buses, and instilled a strong work ethic and national unity. It also mandated the prominent display of the national flag and the singing of the national anthem in schools.

74626.subject: Government
74626.question_text: A bicameral legislature is made up of
74626.explanation: A bicameral legislature is a system of government in which the legislative branch is divided into two separate houses or chambers, such as a Senate and a House of Representatives.

74627.subject: Government
74627.question_text: Colonial policy of assimilation was introduced in Africa by the
74627.explanation: The French colonial administration famously used the Policy of Assimilation, which aimed to turn African subjects into "Frenchmen" by teaching them French culture, language and laws.

74628.subject: Government
74628.question_text: A confederal system of governance is characterised by
74628.explanation:
A confederal system (or confederation) is a form of governance where power is decentralised. In this system, sovereign states or independent regional governments delegate only limited, specific powers to a weak central authority.

 The regional governments retain their individual sovereignty and independence, often holding the right to secede from the confederation

74629.subject: Government
74629.question_text: Registration of political parties is the responsibility of the
74629.explanation:
In most democratic systems, the Electoral Commission (such as INEC in Nigeria or the FEC in the US) is the independent body legally empowered to oversee the democratic process. Their responsibilities  include:

  • Registering political parties: Ensuring they meet legal requirements to exist.

  • Conducting elections: Organising the voting process and announcing results.

  • Voter registration: Maintaining the database of eligible voters.

  • Monitoring party finances: Ensuring parties follow laws regarding campaign funding.

74630.subject: Government
74630.question_text: Government can ascertain feedback on public policy through
74630.explanation:
In a democratic system, governments use public opinion as a primary tool to understand how citizens feel about current laws and future policies. This feedback loop is essential because:

  • Measuring Effectiveness: Polling and surveys allow agencies to collect targeted data on the quality and impact of public services.

  • Direct Interaction: Public opinion is gauged through methods like citizen satisfaction surveys, town hall meetings, and public consultations, where citizens can voice concerns directly to government representatives.

  • Accountability: It serves as a check on those in power by elevating the concerns of everyday people.

74631.subject: Government
74631.question_text: Which of the following is not an obligation of a citizen?
74631.explanation:
In a democracy, there is a clear distinction between obligations (things you must do) and rights (things you are permitted to do).

Contesting an election is considered a right or privilege (the "right to be voted for"). A citizen can choose to run for office, but they are not legally required to do so.

74632.subject: Government
74632.explanation: A sovereign state has complete self-determination over its internal and external affairs, meaning it does not look beyond its own borders for the source of its legal authority. For a state to be truly sovereign, its government must function without foreign interference or control.

options.text: which sovereignty is vested in the military
whose government decisions are made independent
where its citizens can speak without fear or favour
whose constitution could only be changed by the military government

74633.subject: Government
74633.question_text: An election that allows political parties to choose a flag bearer for general election is called
74633.explanation: A primary election is the process which party members or the public select a candidate to represent that party in a general election. Its purpose is to narrow the field of candidates and determine who will be the official "flag bearer" for the party

74634.subject: Government
74634.question_text: The British company granted the charter to rule and administer the northern area before direct colonial rule was known as
74634.explanation: The Royal Niger Company was a British chartered company that was instrumental in spreading British influence in West Africa. It was granted a royal charter in 1886, giving it authority to rule and administer territories along the Niger River. In 1900, the company handed over its administrative control to the British Crown, leading to the creation of the Northern Nigeria Protectorate.

74635.subject: Government
74635.question_text: Nigeria became a federation of nineteen states in
74635.explanation:
Nigeria’s state structure has evolved significantly since independence. Under the military regime of General Murtala Muhammed, the number of states was increased from 12 to 19. This was done to bring the government closer to the people and address ethnic tensions.

The 1976 decree created seven new states: Bauchi, Benue, Borno, Imo, Niger, Ogun, and Ondo. It also renamed several existing states (e.g., North-Western State became Sokoto and Niger).

It was also in 1976 that the decision was made to move the capital from Lagos to Abuja, designating it as the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

74636.subject: Government
74636.question_text: The head of the legislative arm at the third tier of government in Nigeria is the
74636.explanation:
Nigeria operates a three-tier system of government: Federal, State and Local. Each tier has its own executive and legislative branches to ensure the separation of powers.

At the local level, the legislative arm consists of elected Councillors. While the executive arm is headed by the Chairman, the legislative arm (the Council) is presided over by one of the councillors who is elected by their peers to serve as the Leader of the House (or Council Leader). The Leader coordinates the making of "bye-laws," which are the specific laws governing the local government area.

74637.subject: Government
74637.question_text: Political power in a democracy is derived from the
74637.explanation:
Democracy is literally defined as "rule of the people" (from the Greek demos meaning people and kratos meaning power).  In a democratic system, the citizens of the country are the only source of power.

People exercise this power by electing representatives to govern on their behalf. This is often summarized by the phrase "government of the people, by the people, and for the people".

74638.subject: Government
74638.question_text: The Secretariat of the Commonwealth of Nations is located in
74638.explanation: The international headquarters of the Commonwealth Secretariat is located in Marlborough House. Marlborough House is situated on Pall Mall in London, United Kingdom. It has served as the Commonwealth's headquarters since 1959 and hosts various independence negotiations and high-level conferences.

74639.subject: Government
74639.question_text: By composition, ECOWAS can be regarded as a
74639.explanation: ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States) is a group of fifteen countries located specifically in the West African sub-region. It was founded in 1975 to promote economic integration and cooperation among these neighboring countries. It is considered one of the regional pillars of the broader African Economic Community.

74640.subject: Government
74640.question_text: The recruitment, promotion and discipline of civil servants is a key function of the
74640.explanation:
Under the Nigerian Constitution, the Federal Civil Service Commission (FCSC) has the sole authority to appoint, promote and discipline federal civil servants.

It sets uniform guidelines for staff management and serves as an appellate body for petitions regarding employment matters within the civil service. Its functions are designed to ensure that recruitment and progression are based on merit while adhering to the Federal Character principle.

74641.subject: Government
74641.question_text: The umbrella body for relations among all African countries is
74641.explanation: The African Union (AU) is the primary continental organisation of African states. It consists of the 55 member states that make up the countries of the African continent. It was officially launched in 2002 as the successor to the Organisation of African Unity (OAU).

74642.subject: Government
74642.explanation: A party coalition occurs when multiple political parties join together to form a governing alliance. This is common in multi-party systems where no single party wins an absolute majority of seats in the legislature.

74643.subject: Government
74643.question_text: The Babangida transition programme to civil rule officially started in
74643.explanation: The Babangida transition programme to civil rule officially started in 1987. General Ibrahim Babangida launched the political transition program in July 1987, which included the creation of two political parties (NRC and SDP).

74644.subject: Government
74644.question_text: A system of government that allows executive powers to be vested in one person
74644.explanation: A system of government that allows executive powers to be vested in one person is the Presidential System. In this system, a single head of government (the President) leads an executive branch that is separate from the legislature.

74663.subject: Government
74663.explanation: Public corporations (also known as state-owned enterprises or statutory bodies) are business organisations established by an Act of Parliament or the government to provide essential services to the public. Because they are owned by the state, their primary source of initial capital and ongoing financial support comes from government grants, budgetary allocations or loans.

74664.subject: Government
74664.question_text: The Casablanca group in the formation of the OAU was known as
74664.explanation:
The Casablanca Group, formed in January 1961, was a bloc of African states, including Ghana, Guinea, Mali, Egypt, and Morocco, that was widely known for its radical approach to Pan-Africanism.

Led by prominent figures like Kwame Nkrumah of Ghana, the group advocated for:

  • Immediate Political Unification: They believed Africa should form a single, politically united federation immediately, referred to as the "United States of Africa".

  • A Supranational Authority: They proposed transferring significant powers from individual national governments to a central African authority.

  • A Unified Military: Nkrumah famously argued for a pan-African army to fight colonialism and protect the continent's sovereignty.

  • Deep Integration: They wanted a common currency, a central bank and a unified market right away.

74665.subject: Government
74665.question_text: Public opinion  is difficult to measure because it can be
74665.explanation:
Measuring public opinion is an inexact science highly susceptible to manipulation through various means:

  • Leading Questions: Pollsters can frame or word questions in a biased way to "manufacture" a desired response.

  • Media and Elite Influence: Politicians and interest groups often use rhetoric, advertising or misinformation to sway public perception before it is even measured.

  • Social Desirability: Respondents may lie or provide "insincere" answers to appear informed or to align with what they think is socially acceptable, making it hard to capture true beliefs.

74666.subject: Government
74666.question_text: When a pressure group is made up of people of the same profession, it is called
74666.explanation: An occupation (or professional) group consists of individuals who share the same vocation and organise to protect their professional interests. Common examples include the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) for lawyers or the Nigerian Union of Teachers (NUT).

74667.subject: Government
74667.question_text: The application of the rule of law can be hindered by
74667.explanation: The rule of law requires that every person is equal before the law. Diplomatic immunity creates a hindrance to this principle because it legally exempts foreign diplomats from the criminal and civil jurisdiction of their host country.

74668.subject: Government
74668.question_text: The Nigerian military cited which of the reasons for taking over the government in the country?
74668.explanation: The Nigerian military cited mismanagement of public funds by the elected political leaders as a reason for taking over the government. Military coup makers accused civilian administrations of being "infested with corruption" and gross mismanagement of national resources. They claimed their intervention was necessary to "return sanity" to public governance and rid the country of "political profiteers" and "swindlers".

options.text: poor funding of military operations and a lack of allocation
mismanagement of public funds by the elected political leaders
intervention of foreign nations in Nigeria's politics and public fund
lack of credible political leaders and political party system

74669.subject: Government
74669.question_text: Adjudication is the primary responsibility of the
74669.explanation: Adjudication is the formal process by which a judge or court resolves legal disputes and interprets laws to reach a verdict. Under the doctrine of separation of powers, the Judiciary adjudicates (interprets laws), the Legislature makes laws and the Executive enforces them.

74670.subject: Government
74670.question_text: Which of the following promotes private ownership of properties?
74670.explanation: Capitalism is an economic system fundamentally based on private ownership of the means of production and the pursuit of individual profit. In socialism or communalism, ownership is typically collective or state-managed rather than private.

74671.subject: Government
74671.question_text: The fundamental objective guiding a nation's foreign policy is
74671.explanation: Foreign policy consists of the strategies a state uses to interact with other nations. All specific foreign policy goals, such as defence, security and economic benefit, are ultimately shaped by the overarching national interest of the state.

74672.subject: Government
74672.question_text: The maintenance of peace, order and cleanliness in Igbo society was a function of
74672.explanation: Traditionally, the age-grade system (uke) in Igboland was responsible for crime prevention, law enforcement, sanitation and community development. They served as a formal mechanism for resolving conflicts and ensuring the stability and cleanliness of the community.

74673.subject: Government
74673.question_text: A law made by local government and public corporation and empowered by an Act of Parliament is
74673.explanation: A bye-law is a set of rules established by a non-sovereign body (like a municipality or corporation) to regulate itself as allowed by a higher authority, such as an Act of Parliament.

74674.subject: Government
74674.question_text: The party system that was operational in Nigeria under the aborted Third Republic was the
74674.explanation: Under the transition program of General Ibrahim Babangida for the Third Republic, the military government decreed a two-party system consisting of only the Social Democratic Party (SDP) and the National Republican Convention (NRC).

74675.subject: Government
74675.question_text: Decentralisation of power is a feature of a
74675.explanation: In a federal state, power is constitutionally shared and decentralised between a central government and sub-national units (like states or provinces), ensuring that no single level of government has absolute control.

74676.subject: Government
74676.explanation:
Written constitutions are generally considered rigid because they require a special, difficult, legal process to be amended, unlike ordinary laws.

While it is common for written constitutions to be rigid, they can occasionally be flexible. For example, New Zealand has a written constitution (composed of various statutes like the Constitution Act 1986) that is considered flexible because it can be amended by a simple majority vote in Parliament, much like ordinary legislation.

74677.subject: Government
74677.explanation: A permanent civil service is composed of non-political, career officials who remain in office even when elected governments change. Their permanence ensures that administrative expertise and the day-to-day functions of the state continue smoothly during transitions between different political administrations.

74678.subject: Government
74678.question_text: A politically independent nation is referred to as a
74678.explanation:
A state is defined as a politically organised community that possesses sovereignty (political independence) over a specific territory and population.

Key Characteristics of a State

For a "politically independent nation" to be classified as a state, it generally must possess four essential elements:

  • Population: A permanent group of people residing within its borders.

  • Territory: A clearly defined geographical area with recognised boundaries.

  • Government: An organised political machinery through which the state’s will is formulated and expressed.

  • Sovereignty: The supreme authority to make and enforce laws without interference from any external power.

74680.subject: Government
74680.question_text: Before the 1976 reforms, local government administration in Nigeria was characterised by
74680.explanation: Before 1976, local governments in Nigeria were not uniform and lacked power. They were heavily controlled by the state (regional) governments and traditional authorities. This high centralisation at the state level meant that local councils had very little independence or functional capacity.

74681.subject: Government
74681.question_text: One of the gains of the nationalist struggles in Nigeria was
74681.explanation:
One of the most significant gains and tools of the nationalist movement in Nigeria was the formation of political parties, which provided a structured platform to agitate for self-rule.

The introduction of the elective principle in the 1922 Clifford Constitution led to the formation of Nigeria’s first political party, the Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP), founded by Herbert Macaulay in 1923.

These parties (such as the NCNC, Action Group, and NPC) were essential for mobilising the masses, increasing political consciousness and negotiating constitutional reforms that eventually led to independence on October 1, 1960.

The struggles also resulted in increased Nigerian participation in governance, higher education (like Yaba Higher College), and constitutional changes that shifted power from the British to Nigerians.

74684.subject: Government
74684.question_text: The minister of defence in Hausa pre-colonial political system is
74684.explanation:
In the highly centralised Hausa/Fulani emirate system, the Emir was assisted by several ministers with specific roles:

  • Madawaki (or Madaki): He was the commander of the army and acted as the Minister of Defense.

  • Galadima: He was the administrator of the capital city.

  • Sarkin Pawa: He was the head of all butchers.

  • Dogari: He served as the head of the police or royal bodyguards.

74685.subject: Government
74685.question_text: A type of government defined by equal representation, credible elections and the sanctity of the ballot box is
74685.explanation:
Democracy is a system of government based on the principle that power belongs to the people. It is characterised by:

  • Equal Representation: Every citizen has an equal opportunity to influence decisions through representatives.

  • Credible Elections: Periodic, free and fair elections allow the public to choose their leaders.

  • Sanctity of the Ballot Box: This refers to the protection of the voting process (such as the use of a secret ballot) to ensure the results accurately reflect the will of the people.

74687.subject: Government
74687.question_text: A remarkable feature of the Republican Constitution was the
74687.explanation:
The 1963 Republican Constitution ended Nigeria's relationship with the British monarchy; the Queen of England was no longer the head of state and was replaced by an elected President.

While the president became the head of state, the Prime Minister remained the head of government, as the constitution retained the parliamentary system. Another key feature was making the Supreme Court of Nigeria the final court of appeal, replacing the British Privy Council.

options.text: The president was the head of government
The prime minister also performs ceremonial functions
Privy Court was the final court of arbiter
The queen ceased to be the Head of State

74688.subject: Government
74688.question_text: The declaration of Africa as the centrepiece of Nigeria's foreign policy could be traced back to the administration of
74688.explanation:
While General Yakubu Gowon's regime is often credited with formalising the "centrepiece" terminology in the 1970s, the policy itself was rooted in the administration of Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa.

Upon independence in 1960, Balewa declared that Africa would be the primary concern of Nigeria's foreign policy. His commitment was evidenced by his leading role in forming the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) in 1963.

74689.subject: Government
74689.explanation: Unlike private enterprises, which are established to make profit, public corporations (like the old NEPA or Water Boards) are created by the government to provide social and essential services at affordable rates to the citizens.

74690.subject: Government
74690.question_text: OPEC was formed by some oil producing nations in
74690.explanation: The Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) was founded in September 1960 at the Baghdad Conference by five founding members: Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela.

74691.subject: Government
74691.question_text: The constitution that allowed forty-six legislative members was the
74691.explanation:
A new Legislative Council was established exclusively for Southern Nigeria under the Clifford Constitution. It consisted of:

  • 46 members in total.
    • 27 official members (colonial administrators).
    • 19 unofficial members, including:
      • 9 Europeans (mainly representatives of commercial interests).
      • 10 Africans
        • 4 were elected (3 elected from Lagos, 1 from Calabar).
        • 6 were appointed by the governor to represent other parts of the country

74692.subject: Government
74692.explanation: In Nigeria, the Ombudsman is represented by the Public Complaints Commission (PCC). Its role is to investigate and resolve complaints by citizens against administrative injustice or the abuse of power by government officials.
